messages:
Ilana: Quick thought: we need a principled pattern for routing requests across hosted/dedicated/private without ever forwarding tenant secrets.
Ilana: Use case: on-prem control plane wants to receive traffic for some tenants but fall back to hosted when capacity fails. How do we keep secrets inside the private boundary? :lock:
Matt: Two options that come up often: ephemeral proxy creds (hosted mints a short-lived credential and forwards it) vs. secret references that force remote runtimes to fetch from their own KMS.
Toma: Strong +1 for secret references. Ephemeral forwarding means we have to be PCI/PII-level careful. If the private runtime can fetch from its KMS based on a signed policy token, we never transmit raw creds.
Ben: Practicality: we need a manifest-level extension for this. Something like:
```
manifest:
  secrets:
    - name: MODEL_KEY
      ref: secret://tenant/keys/model
      strategy: reference
  routing:
    privileged_routing: true
    on_unreachable: degrade_local
```
But encode allowed failover behaviors per tenant (deny, fallback-to-hosted, queue).
Ilana: Important: "degrade_local" is risky for regulated tenants. We need per-tenant defaults and legal signoff for which fallbacks are allowed.
Matt: I propose a signed proof token pattern: control plane issues a short JWT that asserts the tenant policy (claims: tenant_id, secret_strategy=reference, allowed_failover=queue) signed by control plane key. Edge attaches this to the request. Runtime verifies token and uses its identity to fetch secrets. Edge never carries secrets.
Toma: That would also solve auditing: token includes nonce + request id so we can trace which side requested secret fetches. But we must solve key rotation and TTLs, and ensure runtime can verify without constant CP calls.
Ben: Implementation details to track:
- verifier rotation: we need a JWKS endpoint and rotation window
- TTLs: very short to limit replay
- clock skew: add grace window and NTP checks
- audit: runtime should emit event when secret fetch happens (who asked, proof token id)
Ilana: Network partitions: what should happen if the runtime cannot reach its KMS? For high-compliance tenants it should fail hard (503). For others maybe we allow hosted fallback but only if tenant opted in. So manifest needs on_unreachable: [fail, fallback_hosted, queue].
Matt: Also note streaming semantics: long-stream calls complicate queuing. If we queue at edge and then fallback, clients may see odd latencies. We should prefer fast failure with a clear error code and let clients retry with backoff unless tenant explicitly opted into queued async behavior.
Toma: We also need a small capability-probing handshake for runtimes when registering: record which KMS/backends are accessible and what fallback modes they permit. That can be in the runtime registration payload and used by the edge to evaluate routing decisions.
Ben: Observability lines:
- routing_decision: privileged->private
- secret_strategy: reference
- proof_token_id: <id>
- outcome: success | kms_unreachable | rejected_policy
- fetch_actor: runtime | control-plane
That way audits show whether secret was fetched locally or proxy.
Ilana: Action items:
- Toma: PR for manifest schema additions: secret refs + on_unreachable and allowed_failovers. (link to draft in ticket comment)
- Matt: prototype proof-token issuer + verifier lib (node + go) and rotation docs
- Ben: add trace fields & audit event definitions to observability docs
- Ilana: sync legal on allowed default fallbacks for regulated tenants
ops-bot: Deploybot: created ticket INF-5234 for prototype work (https://tracker/redwood/INF-5234)
Matt: I'll pair with Toma Tuesday to get the token PoC wired up.
Ilana: If we need more formalization we can spin an RFC, but let's try the prototype first. :thumbsup:
